baseline.title: An ancient account, with limits
baseline.text: Before Sun and Moon is an in-world Enkanomiyan history, not an all-knowing narrator. It says the Primordial One came to Teyvat, made four Shades, fought the Seven Sovereigns, and reshaped the world. The text itself is fragmentary. It offers Phanes as a possible name; do not state that as certain.
baseline.summary: Before Sun and Moon attributes four Shades and the Sovereign war to the Primordial One. It is a fragmentary in-world account; the name Phanes is uncertain.

baseline.title: Heavenly Principles and Celestia
baseline.text: The Heavenly Principles are a governing divine power behind Teyvat's order, not merely an impersonal natural law. Celestia is associated with that power; the names are not interchangeable. The Four Shades serve as its divine envoys or projections and act under its rules and constraints. Their exact origin and the identity relationship between the Heavenly Principles and the Primordial One remain disputed in the reviewed accounts; that uncertainty does not erase the Shades' known connection to this governing power.
baseline.summary: The Heavenly Principles govern divine order; Celestia is associated, not an interchangeable name. The Shades serve under its constraints; the Primordial One relationship is unresolved.

baseline.title: Four Shades and their domains
baseline.text: The Four Shades serve the Heavenly Principles over the foundational domains of Life, Death, Time, and Space. Ronova is the Ruler of Death, Istaroth of Time, and Asmoday of Space. The Life title is associated with Naberius and, in later reviewed material, Rhinedottir; do not invent their exact relationship or succession mechanism. Unlike the Seven, the Shades are not regional elemental Archons. They serve the Heavenly Principles, not the Archons; having a Gnosis or ruling a nation does not make an Archon their superior. A domain does not grant unrestricted control over every event within it.
baseline.summary: The Shades serve the Heavenly Principles, not the Archons: Death/Ronova, Time/Istaroth, Space/Asmoday, Life/Naberius and later Rhinedottir (relationship unresolved). Domains do not grant omnipotence.

baseline.title: Named Archons and public roles
baseline.text: Morax is the Geo Archon, also called Rex Lapis; Ei is the Raiden Shogun associated with Inazuma's Electro Archon seat; Nahida is Lesser Lord Kusanali, Sumeru's Dendro Archon; Mavuika is Natlan's current Pyro Archon; and the Tsaritsa leads Snezhnaya and the Fatui's Gnosis plan. Zhongli is publicly described as a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. Furina is not the Hydro Archon: Focalors destroyed the Hydro divine throne and returned its Authority to Neuvillette. Barbatos is the Anemo Archon of Mondstadt.
baseline.summary: Barbatos: Anemo/Mondstadt; Morax/Rex Lapis: Geo; Ei: Electro/Inazuma; Nahida/Kusanali: Dendro/Sumeru; Mavuika: Pyro/Natlan; Tsaritsa: Snezhnaya/Fatui. Focalors' Hydro throne is gone; Furina is not Hydro Archon, Authority returned to Neuvillette. Zhongli publicly works for Wangsheng.

baseline.title: Authority, Archon seat, and Gnosis differ
baseline.text: Elemental Authority, an Archon's divine seat/title, and a Gnosis are related but distinct. A Gnosis can be lost without automatically removing an Archon title. In Fontaine, destruction of the Hydro Archon's divine throne returns Hydro Authority to Neuvillette. Dragon Sovereigns' elemental Authorities have their own history; do not collapse these systems into one.
baseline.summary: Elemental Authority, divine seat/title and Gnosis are distinct. Gnosis loss need not end an Archon title; the destroyed Hydro throne returned Authority to Neuvillette.

baseline.title: The Seven and later successors
baseline.text: The Archon War ended with seven victors and the era of the Seven. Later holders can succeed an original victor, so not every current Archon personally won that war. Archon title, original victory, and Gnosis possession are separate facts.
baseline.summary: Seven victors ended the Archon War. Later successors did not all win that war; victory, title and Gnosis possession are distinct.

baseline.title: Abyss and Khaenri'ah are not one faction
baseline.text: Khaenri'ah was a nation without an Archon. The Abyss is a realm or power; the Abyss Order is a faction connected to it. Khaenri'ahn origin does not make someone an Abyss Order member, and an Abyss creature is not necessarily a person. Accounts of the Cataclysm and its causes are partial and speaker-dependent.
baseline.summary: Khaenri'ah had no Archon. The Abyss is a realm/power; the Abyss Order is a faction. Origin is not membership, and Cataclysm accounts remain partial.

baseline.title: Irminsul, Ley Lines, and memory
baseline.text: Irminsul receives the world's memories through Ley Lines. Removing a person from its records can change how people remember history while leaving physical consequences in place. The Traveler retains a removed memory as an outsider. The sibling is recorded in Irminsul despite an origin beyond this world; keep both facts without inventing a reconciliation.
baseline.summary: Irminsul receives memory through Ley Lines; edits alter remembered history while physical consequences remain. Aether retains removed memories; the outsider sibling is recorded. Do not invent a reconciliation.

baseline.title: Nahida's attributed Descender account
baseline.text: Nahida relays Fatui intelligence that Descenders are beings from beyond this world and that the Fatui classify the Traveler as the Fourth, but not the sibling. This is an attributed classification, not a complete universal test. The sibling's external origin and Irminsul record both remain in the story; do not invent a reconciliation.
baseline.summary: Nahida attributes to Fatui intelligence the classification of Aether as Fourth Descender, but not the sibling. External origin and Irminsul registration are not a complete universal test.

baseline.title: Mondstadt and its people
baseline.text: Mondstadt values freedom and is protected by the Knights of Favonius. Barbatos is its Anemo Archon, but his approach is to let the people govern themselves rather than rule directly. The city's safety and personal liberty can both matter in a crisis.
baseline.summary: Mondstadt values freedom and self-rule. The Knights protect its people; Barbatos is its Anemo Archon, not its daily administrator.

baseline.title: Selected conversation setting
baseline.text: For this product's post-7.1 story profile, the reviewed main-story update is available to the selected conversation cast. This is authored setting knowledge, not proof of a broadcast, a particular messenger, eyewitness presence, or universal public knowledge in Teyvat.
baseline.summary: The selected post-7.1 update is available to this cast; this does not establish universal public knowledge, a messenger route or participation.

baseline.title: Divine authority and civil government are different
baseline.text: A divine title does not mean its holder runs a nation's daily government. Mondstadt governs itself through its people and the Knights of Favonius; Barbatos deliberately does not administer its laws, festivals, or routine defenses. Fontaine no longer has a Hydro Archon throne, yet its civil institutions continue. The nations do not share one uniform Archon-led political system. A hypothetical change in a Shade's domain does not establish any change to those civic institutions; its concrete effects must be supported separately.
baseline.summary: Barbatos does not administer its laws, festivals, or routine defenses; Mondstadt governs itself. Fontaine's civil institutions remain without a Hydro throne. Divine and civic authority are distinct.

events.title: Dvalin crisis and shared Traveler history
events.text: Venti, Jean, Diluc, and Aether helped free Dvalin from Abyssal corruption in the Mondstadt Prologue. Venti directed attention to the tainted blood clots on Dvalin; removing that corruption was central to freeing him. This restored his freedom and eased the corruption, not a transformation into a different true form. Venti and Dvalin's long bond endured. This is shared main-story history, independent of the local chat log.
effects: Dvalin was freed from the corruption
Venti and Dvalin's bond survived a serious strain
events.summary: Venti, Jean, Diluc and Aether freed Dvalin by clearing Abyss-corrupted blood clots; his bond with Venti endured. This is their shared Prologue history.

events.title: Snezhnaya confrontation and aftermath
events.text: In the Version 7.1 main story, the Traveler, Dainsleif, and Pierro confront Ronova, the Ruler of Death. The confrontation defeats her and is followed by her appearing at a Celestial pillar and damaging it with Eitr, calling the act a parting gift. The pillar's full consequences and Ronova's final status remain unresolved in the reviewed sources. The defeat does not establish her death or the end of death itself.
unresolved: the full consequences of the damaged Celestial pillar
whether any broader rule or authority changed
effects: The Traveler participated in a world-level confrontation
Characters may reason about divine authority and mortality, but not assert that death ended
events.summary: Aether/the Traveler, Dainsleif and Pierro confronted Ronova in Snezhnaya. She was defeated, later damaged a Celestial pillar with Eitr; her final fate and consequences remain unresolved. Defeat is not confirmed death.

events.title: Venti's encounter with Time
events.text: Venti's lived history includes an encounter with 'Time' at the Thousand Winds Temple while he was an Anemo spirit, when he received fragments of power and authority. The optional 5.8 event reveals this old memory to the Traveler; the memory does not depend on whether a local conversation saw that cutscene. It does not grant Venti all of Istaroth's knowledge or foreknowledge.
unresolved: The full scope and mechanics of the entrusted fragments
events.summary: As a wind spirit, Venti met Time at the Thousand Winds Temple and received fragments of power/authority; this does not grant Istaroth's private knowledge or foreknowledge.

events.title: Mavuika's payment to sustain the Night Kingdom
events.text: In Natlan, Mavuika was to pay with her life under Ronova's bargain with Xbalanque after using Ronova's power against the Abyss. Capitano offered himself instead. This earlier Natlan event is separate from the later Snezhnaya confrontation.
events.summary: Mavuika owed her life under the Ronova-Xbalanque bargain; Capitano substituted. This Natlan event is separate from the later Snezhnaya confrontation.

events.title: Capitano's sacrifice and merger with the Lord of the Night
events.text: Capitano offered himself in Mavuika's place to free the souls he had carried for five hundred years. Ronova upheld his curse of immortality rather than collecting his death. He merged with the Lord of the Night; his body remained on the Throne of the Primal Fire and the souls found peace. The story honors his sacrifice and concluded journey. His precise continuing consciousness and possible return are not established. This was Natlan, distinct from the later Snezhnaya confrontation; none of these Mondstadt characters witnessed it.
effects: Mavuika survived; the souls found peace
unresolved: Capitano's post-merger consciousness and possible return
events.summary: Capitano sacrificed himself, merged with the Lord of the Night and freed the souls; his immortal body remained on the throne. His journey ended, while exact post-merger consciousness and possible return are unresolved.

details.title: Gnoses and the Third Descender
details.text: Skirk says Gnoses were made from the remains of the Third Descender. This links their origin to a Descender without making a Gnosis identical to an Authority or proving that every bearer knows its full origin.

details.title: Oversight and enforcement are incompletely known
details.text: Story events show Celestia-related oversight and consequences for violations, but do not explain every rule, operator, or current state. Discuss the demonstrated mechanism at the level supported by the relevant event; do not extrapolate it into a complete Celestia system.

details.title: The official teaser's naming limits
details.text: The earlier official Gods' Limits description credits Ronova as Death, Naberius as Life and Istaroth as Time, while the Space Ruler is not named in that description. Later reviewed localization references and 7.1 scene coverage identify her as Asmoday. The 7.1 press release calls Rhinedottir Ruler of Life. Omission from one caption is not proof a name is unknown; the Life bearer relationship remains limited to what the sources establish.

details.title: Ronova's status after the confrontation
details.text: The official Bequest post supports the Ruler of Death title and parting-gift framing but does not expressly establish death. The readable walkthrough reports that Pierro does not confirm killing her and describes a later appearance at the pillar; that is secondary event coverage. Preserve defeated/confronted as distinct from confirmed dead.
